input.title: fragment() on a nested field returns the results of a different field
input.summary: A precise bug report. `Query.fragment()` (tinydb/queries.py:489-501) builds its query hash as `('fragment', freeze(document))` and leaves out `self._path`. The other path-based tests I read (`==`, `any`, `all`, `one_of`) include the path in the hash. As a result `User.home.fragment(d)` and `User.work.fragment(d)` have equal hashes and compare equal. I did not check this against the table's query cache, so the cache link is the reporter's hypothesis. The specification has one agreed core requirement (a search must return the documents matching the queried field, including when an earlier search used a different field with the same fragment document) and one candidate (queries on different paths must not compare equal). It does not design the fix. The verdict is READY-WITH-OPEN-ITEMS, not READY, because the stakeholder mode is `unavailable`. Only P3 questions are open. The issue text contained no instructions aimed at the workflow.

requirements.statement: When a search uses `Query().<field>.fragment(document)`, the system shall return exactly the stored documents whose value at `<field>` contains the key/value pairs of `document`, regardless of whether an earlier search on the same database used a different field with an equal fragment document.
requirements.source_quote: The second search gives me the result of the first one!

acceptance_criteria.given: a TinyDB on MemoryStorage holding {'name': 'ana', 'home': {'city': 'Pune'}, 'work': {'city': 'Delhi'}} and {'name': 'raj', 'home': {'city': 'Delhi'}, 'work': {'city': 'Pune'}}, and a first search `db.search(User.home.fragment({'city': 'Pune'}))` has already run
acceptance_criteria.when: `db.search(User.work.fragment({'city': 'Pune'}))` is called on the same db object
acceptance_criteria.then: the result is a list containing only the 'raj' document

acceptance_criteria.given: the same database and data, with no earlier search
acceptance_criteria.then: the result is a list containing only the 'ana' document

acceptance_criteria.given: the same database and data, with `User.work.fragment({'city': 'Pune'})` searched first
acceptance_criteria.when: `db.search(User.home.fragment({'city': 'Pune'}))` is called on the same db object
acceptance_criteria.then: the result is a list containing only the 'ana' document

acceptance_criteria.given: the same database and data, after `db.search(User.home.fragment({'city': 'Pune'}))` has returned the 'ana' document
acceptance_criteria.when: the identical search is repeated on the same db object
acceptance_criteria.then: the result is again a list containing only the 'ana' document

requirements.statement: The system shall treat `Query().home.fragment({'city': 'Pune'})` and `Query().work.fragment({'city': 'Pune'})` as unequal queries (`==` returns False).
requirements.source_quote: Also `User.home.fragment({...}) == User.work.fragment({...})` is `True`, which surprised me.

interpretations: The table's query result cache returns an entry stored for another query, because the two queries compare equal
Some other stale-state mechanism, since a fresh TinyDB gives the correct result

open_questions.question: Should two fragment queries on different field paths with the same fragment document compare unequal, as FR-QRY-002 states, or is the equality only a symptom of the wrong search result?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The reporter says only that the equality 'surprised' them. Making it a requirement adds negation, so it stays a candidate until the maintainer accepts it.
options: (b) Drop FR-QRY-002 and keep only the search-result requirement

open_questions.question: Should other `Query` methods that use a path be checked for the same problem of leaving the path out of the query hash, or is only `fragment` in scope?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Sets the scope of the fix and tests. Only `fragment` is reported. I read `==`, `any`, `all` and `one_of` and they include the path. I did not read the others.
options: (b) Also audit the remaining path-based methods (e.g. matches, search, test, exists, comparison operators)

assumptions.text: Queries on different field paths with the same fragment document should be unequal (FR-QRY-002).
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: A test for FR-QRY-002 would enforce behaviour the maintainer does not want. The impact is low, because equality of queries on different paths is hard to justify.

assumptions.text: The reporter's environment (tinydb 4.9.0, Python 3.12, Windows 11) is context only. The behaviour is platform-independent and can be reproduced with MemoryStorage.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: A platform-specific cause would not be reproduced by the pytest tests.

assumptions.text: The requester/maintainer is the decision owner for scope. No maintainer comments were supplied, so the stakeholder mode is `unavailable`.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: The scope decisions in Q-001 and Q-002 may be made by someone else.

out_of_scope: Designing or choosing the fix (for example how the hash or cache key is built)
Redesigning or removing the query cache
Changing the behaviour of query methods other than fragment unless Q-002 is answered otherwise
Changes to documentation or the public API
